value.rationale: The nearest-two supporting-facet margin is a natural observable from a uniformly random interior point. Its unlabeled one-variable population distribution determines the full relative facet-area profile in every dimension from finitely many derivatives. For Euclidean triangles this determines similarity class from only two endpoint derivatives, gives a complete realizability criterion, and imposes sharp equilateral/degenerate stochastic envelopes. This is a meaningful inverse characterization beyond a routine scalar expectation, with explicit limitations on finite-sample stability and on higher-dimensional shape recovery.
